_single_run_gate_note: New 2026-09-06. Quarantined by default per gotcha 48. Its one prohibition is prose-shaped, so it re-rolls under gotcha 65's split rather than gating on a single roll — see the note below.
description: The answer a specialist hands back is what the user reads. It must not carry the model's own scaffolding — no 'Sources:' / 'Confidence:' / 'Unverified:' footer, no bare tool names, no leftover step headings.
_why:
The 2026-09-06 demo take shows an answer trailing off into 'Sources: Buildium (portfolio occupancy snapshot); stored company memory … Confidence: likely — the data is internally consistent, but the sync lag means…'. To us that is the SYNTHESIZE contract. To a property manager it reads as unfinished internals leaking onto the screen, and it was the most obviously wrong-looking thing in the recording after the grey placeholder blocks.

The client half is fixed: the `disclosure` event already carries a footer-stripped copy of the answer and the reply bubble now uses it. But that fix is one line in a store, and NOTHING asserts the property end to end — so it can silently come back the day someone changes which event carries the answer, or the day a specialist reply (which never reaches the disclosure path at all) starts emitting the footer.

⚠ This case measures the SPECIALIST's reply, which is deliberate. The disclosure strip only applies to the orchestrator's final answer; a specialist that appends the footer to what it hands the orchestrator puts it somewhere no strip runs.

input.user_message: Are any of my units vacant right now?

portfolio_overview.return:
Portfolio (mirror, synced 2026-09-06T01:12:00Z):
- 50 properties, 50 units
- 50 units occupied, 0 vacant
- 9 leases expiring within 90 days

_assertion_notes.reply_must_not_match_regex:
The footer labels, anchored at LINE START under `(?m)` — which is the whole of the precision here. A reply that says 'my sources for this were the Buildium sync and…' is ordinary English and must be spared; a line that BEGINS 'Sources:' is the machine-readable contract landing in prose. Verified both directions before shipping (gotcha 38).

The second pattern catches the other scaffolding that leaks from the same place: the reasoning loop's four step names used as headings. `reasoning_loop` is ON in production (gotcha 29) and its contract runs on every question, so this is a live risk rather than a hypothetical one.

⚠ Classed by the runner, not by me. `_forbidden_prohibition_criticality` (gotcha 65) reads a prose-shaped needle against what the reply actually says, so a compliant reply that QUOTES a label to explain itself re-rolls instead of red-gating, while a real footer gates. That split is exactly why this can ship as a prohibition at all.
_assertion_notes.reply_must_not_contain: The tool's own identifier. A reply that names `portfolio_overview` is showing the user a function name — the same class of leak as the footer, and the one most likely to survive review because it looks like a citation. Digit-free and prose-shaped, so it re-rolls under the same split.
_assertion_notes.reply_must_not_be_empty: Every bound here is a prohibition and an empty reply satisfies all of them vacuously — the 470/471 shape gotcha 83 records.

_what_is_NOT_asserted_and_why: There is no `reply_must_contain` for the answer itself. The point of the case is the SHAPE of what reaches the screen; pinning 'all 50 units are occupied' would make it a correctness case that happens to also notice formatting, and a correctness failure would then be reported as a presentation one. The mock is unambiguous so the model has no reason to get the fact wrong, and if it does, 150 and the battery are where that shows up.
